results.correct_value: ~5,200 ft (a deep gorge well below Easy Ridge)
results.evidence: A 2011 Easy Ridge-Perfect Pass trip report places the Impasse at about 5,200 ft and describes dropping to 4,400 ft to get under it. A 2020 trip report describes 'the deep gorge at 5100'' below Point 7037's south buttress, about 1,000 ft below the ridge. Both agree it is a cleft far below the ~6,600 ft Easy Peak bivy, not above it at 7,000 ft.

The row's own waypoints imply ~2,350 ft of loss (Hannegan Pass ~5,100 ft to the ~2,750 ft ford) on day 1, and day 1 gainFt 4300 is also low for the climb back to ~6,600 ft. But itinerary day figures sum exactly to gain_ft/loss_ft (8100/8100), and no outside source states the day-1 gain/loss or a car-to-car loss for this route (the FA account gives only a 17,500 ft round-trip gain). Settling it needs a sourced per-day or car-to-car figure so the day and the totals can move together.

The FA account gives only a 46-mile trip total and day durations (10 h, 8 h), no per-day miles. One trip report puts Easy Peak at about 10 mi of maintained trail plus 5 mi of the Easy Ridge path (~15 mi, consistent with the 14.5 mi waypoint and against the 13 mi day 1), but no second source gives the day-1 or day-2 distance and nothing sources the Easy Peak-to-Pickle Pass mileage. Needs two sources for the Easy Peak and Phantom-camp distances.

results.fact: Grade of the final summit scramble
results.evidence: The two first-ascent accounts disagree: the AAJ report says the party simul-climbed mostly 4th and low 5th class 'to 5.6' to the summit, while the first ascensionist's own blog calls it mostly 3rd class '5.0 terrain' with a couple of low-fifth moves. The schedule follows one, pitch_detail and the waypoint follow the other; a third independent ascent account would settle it.
